title: Ceviche Peruano
subtitle: raw fish cured in lime juice with aji amarillo and red onion
excerpt: Peruvian ceviche is good for fresh fish in lime juice with aji amarillo, chilli and red onion. The acid firms the fish and draws out a cloudy, flavour-rich marinade called leche de tigre. It is served cold with sweet potato and corn.
sourceNotes: Ceviche is Peru's national dish and has been prepared along the Pacific coast for thousands of years. Pre-Inca communities cured fish in fermented chicha; limes arrived with Spanish colonists and transformed the marinade. In 2004, the Peruvian government declared ceviche part of the national cultural heritage.

glossaryTerms.definition: Spanish for tiger's milk. The cloudy citrus marinade left in the bowl after the fish has cured. It is drunk as a tonic in Peru and is rich in flavour from the fish, lime juice and chilli.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 as a starter and needs just 20 minutes of preparation plus 15 minutes of chilling. The lime juice is good for 600g of very fresh sea bass or sole, changing its texture from raw to opaque and firm. As the fish is good for, it releases juices that combine with the lime to form
, the intensely flavoured marinade that pools at the bottom of the bowl.

The fish must be extremely fresh. Ask your fishmonger for sushi-grade or day-boat fish if possible. Do not is good for for longer than 15 minutes or the texture becomes rubbery rather than just firm. Slice the red onion as thin as you can manage and soak it in cold salted water for 5 minutes to mellow the bite before adding it to the dish.
Remove the skin from 600g very fresh sea bass or sole and cut the flesh into 2cm cubes. Place in a cold bowl and refrigerate while you prepare the other ingredients.
Soak the thinly sliced red onion in cold salted water for 5 minutes. Drain and pat dry.
In a bowl, combine the lime juice, aji amarillo paste, minced garlic, 1 tsp salt and 1 finely chopped aji limo or bird's-eye chilli. Stir to dissolve the salt.

Add the fish cubes to the lime mixture. Toss gently to coat every piece. Cover and refrigerate for exactly 15 minutes. The fish will turn opaque on the outside while staying slightly translucent at the centre.
Remove from the fridge. Add the drained red onion and coriander leaves. Toss gently once more.
Serve immediately on cold plates with sliced boiled sweet potato and corn. Spoon some of the leche de tigre over the fish and sweet potato before serving.

attrs.cause: It was left in the lime juice too long
attrs.fix: Stick to 15 minutes of curing. Set a timer as soon as the fish goes in.

attrs.symptom: Very little leche de tigre in the bowl
attrs.cause: The fish was not fresh enough to release much liquid
attrs.fix: Use the freshest fish available. Adding an extra lime squeezed over at serving also helps boost the volume of marinade.

attrs.cause: The onion was not soaked before adding
attrs.fix: Always soak sliced red onion in cold salted water for at least 5 minutes and drain well before mixing into the ceviche.

content.text: Ceviche is Peru's national dish and is eaten at lunch rather than dinner. Cevicherias open in the morning and often sell out by early afternoon. It is a dish built around the Pacific coast and the extraordinary freshness of the fish caught there.
